text_blocks.snippet: Search interest and consumer demand for solar panels in India are growing at an unprecedented pace. This surge is reflected in digital lookups, market investment, and record-breaking infrastructure expansion. In 2025, India overtook the United States to become the world’s second-largest market for annual solar capacity additions. By mid-2026, India's total installed solar capacity reached nearly 165 GW, a massive jump from just 2.8 GW in 2014.
snippet_highlighted_words: Search interest and consumer demand for solar panels in India are growing at an unprecedented pace.

text_blocks.snippet: The accelerating growth timeline is driven by structural shifts, economic factors, and major policy changes.
Key Drivers of Growth Over Time
Data tracking consumer behavior reveals a steep rise in retail solar interest across the country.

list.snippet: Rising Search Intent: Online searches for solar panel dealers surged by 173%, while searches for solar panel cleaning and maintenance services doubled (+100%).

Regional Spikes: Cities like Delhi (+92%), Lucknow (+77%), and Ahmedabad (+63%) have registered the sharpest rises in solar service interest, showing that demand has moved heavily into residential and commercial urban hubs.

text_blocks.snippet: 2. The Impact of "PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana"
Launched in early 2024, this mega government subsidy program has supercharged public interest by aiming to provide rooftop solar to 1 crore (10 million) households.

list.snippet: As of mid-2026, over 51 lakh (5.1 million) families have already been empowered by the scheme.
Over 9.56 GW of rooftop solar capacity was installed by early 2026 alone, making distributed clean energy accessible to the middle class.

text_blocks.snippet: India has emerged as one of the most competitive solar markets globally due to highly optimized generation costs.

list.snippet: The levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) for utility solar projects in India fell to $35 per megawatt-hour.

This makes solar power in India cheaper than in China ($36/MWh) and dramatically cheaper than in the US ($62/MWh), pushing private businesses and state corporations to quickly transition away from traditional coal grids.

text_blocks.snippet: To keep pace with the massive domestic demand and insulate the market from supply chain vulnerabilities, India drastically expanded its industrial capabilities via the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.

list.snippet: Solar module manufacturing capacity skyrocketed from a meager 2.3 GW in 2014 to roughly 172 GW.

text_blocks.snippet: The momentum is projected to continue through the end of the decade. Driven by a national mandate to hit 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, industry analysts predict the broader Indian solar panel market will expand at a CAGR of over 19% to 22% over the next several years, shifting focus toward next-generation battery energy storage systems (BESS) and expanded grid transmission.

For comprehensive breakdowns of current infrastructure policies, updates are published regularly on the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) Portal and the official tracking pages of the Press Information Bureau (PIB).
